metaDescription: Five portable chargers compared on capacity, charging speed, built-in cables and flight rules, from a mini 10000mAh bank to a 50000mAh all-in-one.
introParagraphs: A portable charger is one of those gadgets you only notice when it is missing, and the right one depends on how you use your phone. This lineup runs from the INIU Mini, roughly the size of an AirPods Pro case, to the LHUOED with a 50000mAh battery and a built-in wall plug. In between sit the INIU 10000mAh with 45W output, the Miady 2-pack and the GrnOas.E with two built-in cables.

Capacity numbers can mislead. A 10000mAh bank is about 37 watt-hours at the usual 3.7 volts, a size that is well inside airline limits, while a 50000mAh bank works out to roughly 185 watt-hours, which is above the common 160 watt-hour ceiling for carrying in the cabin. Speed matters just as much: the INIU units list 45W, the GrnOas.E and LHUOED list 22.5W, and the Miady relies on standard USB-C and USB-A outputs.

We evaluated each pick from specs, listed features and buyer feedback rather than hands-on testing, and weighted portability, built-in cables and safe travel use. If you fly with a charger, keep it in your carry-on, look for a printed watt-hour rating, and check your airline's rules before packing.

products.name: INIU 10000mAh 45W Portable Charger
products.description:
The INIU 10000mAh balances speed, size and travel rules better than anything else here. It lists 45W output, enough to push an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 76 percent or an iPad Pro to 60 percent in the time the listing quotes. The battery uses a high-density cell that makes it 40 percent smaller and lighter than comparable banks.

Its cable is detachable, a design that sets it apart from banks with built-in cords. If the cord frays you can swap it, and the same short USB-C cable works for other devices. The tradeoff is that you must carry that cable, so it is a little less self-contained than the GrnOas.E. It sits in the middle of the price range.

At 10000mAh it is about 37 watt-hours, well inside the 100 watt-hour cabin limit, and it is labeled flight-safe. Compared with the INIU Mini, it is a bit larger but the same capacity and speed. Compared with the LHUOED, it is far lighter, which matters for daily carry.
products.bestFor: Most people who want fast, flight-friendly charging in a compact body.
pros: 45W output charges phones and tablets quickly
About 40 percent smaller than comparable banks
cons: You have to keep track of the detachable cable

products.name: INIU Mini 10000mAh 45W Portable Charger

specList.label: Size
specList.value: About the size of an AirPods Pro case

products.description:
The INIU Mini packs 10000mAh and 45W output into a body about the size of an AirPods Pro case. That makes it the easiest bank here to drop in a pocket or a small purse. The listing claims it can take a Samsung S26 Ultra from 20 percent quickly with its fast output.

Its detachable nylon-braided USB-C lanyard cable is a small convenience, since it is designed to outlast standard cords. The tradeoff is that the small size leaves less room for built-in ports or cables, so you rely on that one lanyard. It sits in a high price tier compared with the budget banks.

As with the INIU 10000mAh, it works out to about 37 watt-hours at 3.7 volts, inside the airline limit, and it is described as flight-safe. Compared with the INIU 10000mAh, the Mini is smaller, and compared with the Miady, it charges faster but includes only one bank. Choose it if pocketability is your priority.
products.bestFor: People who want the smallest 10000mAh bank with fast output.
pros: About the size of an AirPods Pro case
cons: Single detachable cable to keep track of
High price tier for a small bank

products.name: Miady 2-Pack 10000mAh Portable Charger
products.description:
The Miady is a two-pack of slim 10000mAh banks, which means you can keep one at home and one in your bag. Each bank has three outputs and two inputs, so you can charge up to three devices at once, such as a phone, tablet and earbuds. The USB-C port works for both charging the bank and charging a device.

The tradeoff is speed and cables. The listing emphasizes multiple outputs rather than a headline wattage, and it does not include built-in cables, so you bring your own. It sits at the second-lowest price tier, which makes the pair an efficient purchase.

Two 10000mAh banks give you 20000mAh of total capacity in two flight-friendly units, each about 37 watt-hours. That is easier to travel with than one huge bank. Compared with the INIU, the Miady is slower but gives you two banks, and compared with the GrnOas.E, it has no built-in cables.
products.bestFor: People who want two slim banks for home and travel at a low price tier.
pros: Two banks for the price tier
USB-C works for input and output
Each bank stays within flight limits

products.name: GrnOas.E 10000mAh 22.5W Power Bank
products.description:
The GrnOas.E is the grab-and-go option, with two built-in cables for iPhone and USB-C devices. It combines PD and QC fast charging at 22.5W, and with its USB-C port and extra outputs it can charge four devices at once. No separate cord means nothing to forget.

The tradeoff is that built-in cables cannot be replaced if they fray, and 22.5W is slower than the INIU banks. It sits at the lowest price tier here, so it is an easy pick for a first charger or a spare. Quality control is a bigger variable for lesser-known brands.

At 10000mAh it is about 37 watt-hours and within cabin limits. Compared with the Miady, it includes cables and a faster listed output, and compared with the INIU, it is slower but more self-contained. Choose it if you hate carrying a cord.
products.bestFor: People who want a cheap bank with cables already built in.
pros: Two built-in cables, nothing extra to carry
cons: Built-in cables cannot be swapped if damaged

products.name: LHUOED 50000mAh Portable Charger
products.description:
The LHUOED is the capacity champion, with a 50000mAh battery that lists up to 8.5 recharges of an iPhone 17 Pro Max. It combines a wall charger, built-in cables and a 22.5W USB-C output in one unit, backed by a 3-year warranty. For camping, power outages or long trips, nothing else here comes close.

The catch is airline rules. At the usual 3.7 volts, 50000mAh works out to about 185 watt-hours, above the common 160 watt-hour limit, so it is generally not allowed in the cabin. It is also heavy and sits at the highest price tier, so it is overkill for everyday use.

It makes sense as a home or car backup. Compared with the INIU, it holds five times the capacity but is far less portable, and compared with the Miady, it is one big unit instead of two small ones. Choose it only if you will not fly with it.
products.bestFor: Road trips, outages and camping where capacity matters more than weight.
cons: Roughly 185 Wh, generally too large for flights

buyingCriteria.explanation: Watt-hours equal mAh divided by 1000, multiplied by the battery voltage, usually 3.6 to 3.7 volts. The 10000mAh INIU and GrnOas.E work out to about 37 Wh, while the 50000mAh LHUOED is about 185 Wh. Airlines allow banks up to 100 Wh in the cabin without approval. Always look for a printed Wh rating.

Banks of 100 Wh or less go in the cabin without approval, 100 to 160 Wh need airline approval, usually limited to two, and above 160 Wh are not allowed. Every 10000mAh pick here fits easily, while the LHUOED at roughly 185 Wh does not. Carry banks in your cabin bag, not checked luggage. Check your airline before you fly.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Expect less than the rated capacity
buyingCriteria.explanation: Real output is lower than the label because of conversion losses. Independent tests show roughly 77 to 83 percent of rated capacity is usable. A 10000mAh INIU therefore delivers closer to 8000mAh worth of charge. Plan around that number.

Speed depends on watts. USB-C PD spans 18 to 100 W, while typical USB-A ports deliver 5 to 12 W. The INIU banks list 45W, the GrnOas.E and LHUOED 22.5W. Use the fastest port and a short quality cable.

Built-in cables like the GrnOas.E mean nothing to forget but nothing to replace. The INIU detachable cable can be swapped when it frays. Pick based on how you hate losing things. A spare cable is cheap insurance.

Look for UL or FCC marks and protection against overcharge and short circuits. Lesser-known brands vary in quality control. A warranty such as the LHUOED's 3 years is a helpful signal. Avoid unlabeled banks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and travel rules
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted capacity to watt-hours and compared against airline limits. The 10000mAh picks land near 37 Wh, while the LHUOED lands near 185 Wh. Figures are based on listed specs and standard voltage assumptions, not lab measurement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging speed
howWeEvaluated.description: The INIU banks lead at 45W, while the GrnOas.E and LHUOED list 22.5W. The most basic pick for speed is the Miady, which lists no headline wattage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: The INIU Mini is the smallest at about the size of an AirPods Pro case, and the LHUOED is the largest. Portability drives daily use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cables and ports
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked built-in cables, detachable options and number of outputs. The GrnOas.E offers two built-in cables, the Miady offers three outputs per bank. Convenience here varies by habit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: The GrnOas.E is the lowest-cost pick, the Miady gives two banks cheaply, and the INIU Mini and LHUOED cost the most. Features such as a wall plug only earn credit if you will use them.

howToChoose.subheading: Big Bank vs Two Small Banks

cards.label: One big bank
cards.text: The LHUOED holds 50000mAh in one unit, great for outages. It is heavy and about 185 Wh, so it generally cannot fly.

cards.label: Two small banks
cards.text: The Miady gives two 10000mAh banks, each flight-friendly, so one stays home and one travels.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: choose the Miady for flexibility and the LHUOED only for ground use.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A printed Wh rating at or under 100 Wh, and pack it in your cabin bag. Check your airline.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The INIU 10000mAh 45W Portable Charger is about 37 Wh and labeled flight-safe, making it the best flying companion.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want fast 45W charging and a compact body, in which case the INIU picks justify the price.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only top up now and then. The GrnOas.E offers built-in cables at the lowest price tier.

faq.q: How do I choose between these portable chargers?
faq.a: Start with how you use it. For daily carry, pick a 10000mAh bank like the INIU. For flights, stay under 100 Wh. For outages, consider the LHUOED.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a portable charger?
faq.a: You do not need to spend much. The GrnOas.E and Miady sit at the lowest tiers. Pay more for 45W speed or a smaller body.

faq.q: How long do portable chargers last?
faq.a: Batteries slowly lose capacity over hundreds of charge cycles. Avoid heat and full discharge. Replace a bank that swells.

faq.q: Is a bigger mAh number always better?
faq.a: No. A bigger bank is heavier and may exceed airline limits. Compare watt-hours and real needs. A 10000mAh bank gives about two phone charges.

faq.q: Can I take a portable charger on a plane?
faq.a: Yes, in your cabin bag, if it is 100 Wh or less. 100 to 160 Wh needs airline approval. Above 160 Wh is not allowed.
Only if your device supports it. A phone that accepts 20W will not charge faster on 45W. Short quality cables lose less power.
